raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

With MTP `num_speculative_tokens > 1`, the Model Runner V2 autoregressive speculator reuses one
attention-metadata build across draft steps only if every attention group's builder sets
`supports_draft_decode_metadata_update`. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's QSA side-cache builder
(`QSAMetadataBuilder`, backend `QWEN4_EXP_EXP_QSA_STATE`) does not, so the speculator logs

```
Fused multi-step draft decode is not supported by attention backend(s) QWEN4_EXP_EXP_QSA_STATE;
falling back to rebuilding attention metadata between draft steps.
```

and rebuilds metadata on every draft step for the whole model.

This PR opts the QSA builder in. `update_draft_decode_metadata` re-launches the builder's own
`_build_qsa_metadata_kernel` in place on the metadata's persistent tensors, following the
pattern of `DeepseekSparseSWA`'s update, so draft-step metadata (`token_to_req`,
`logical_positions`, `visible_blocks`, `slot_mapping`, and the compressed cache's
`k_work_metadata`) is computed by exactly the code path `build()` uses.

## Changes

- `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/common/qsa_cache.py`
  - Factor the kernel launch out of `build_qsa_metadata_triton` into
    `_launch_qsa_metadata_kernel`, shared by `build()` and the new update. No behavior change
    for `build()`.
  - `QSAForwardMetadata` gains `common_slot_mapping` (the compressed layout reads it to keep
    padded tokens inert) and `num_mapped_tokens` (previously read from `query_start_loc_cpu`,
    which is not capture-safe inside the draft loop).
  - `QSAMetadataBuilder.supports_draft_decode_metadata_update = HAS_TRITON` and
    `update_draft_decode_metadata`. The PyTorch fallback builder keeps the rebuild path.
- `tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py`
  - `test_qsa_draft_decode_metadata_update_matches_rebuild`: for the plain, compressed and
    circular layouts, an in-place update after advancing `seq_lens` by one equals a fresh
    `build()` at `seq_lens + 1`. The sequence lengths cross a compression boundary, so
    `visible_blocks` must change; the test also asserts the update changed state.

`max_seq_len` is intentionally not refreshed: in this model it is only consumed by the prefill
selection path, and the fused draft loop is decode-only.

## Not a duplicate

- #55292 adds `supports_multi_step_drafting = True` to the same builder. That is a different
  capability (the V1 proposer's multi-step validity check, ROCm-gated) and does not add
  in-place draft metadata updates. The two changes touch adjacent lines of the same class and
  should rebase trivially onto each other.
- #54790 does the equivalent for sparse MLA backends under DCP — different backend.
- No open PR sets `supports_draft_decode_metadata_update` for `QSAMetadataBuilder`.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py -v \
    -k "draft_decode_metadata_update or triton_metadata_matches_pytorch or side_metadata_marks or compressed_metadata_keeps or circular_buffer_metadata_keeps or fused_metadata_matches"
pre-commit run --files vllm/models/qwen4_exp/common/qsa_cache.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py
```

## Test Result

- pre-commit (ruff check, ruff format, typos, mypy-3.10, SPDX, forbidden imports,
  check-test-tethering): **passed**.
- pytest on NVIDIA GB10 (SM121), CUDA + Triton, vLLM 0.30.0 image with this change applied:

  ```
  pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py -k "draft_decode_metadata_update or \
      triton_metadata_matches_pytorch or side_metadata_marks or compressed_metadata_keeps or \
      circular_buffer_metadata_keeps or fused_metadata_matches"
  19 passed
  ```

  The new test for all three layouts, plus the neighboring metadata tests that exercise
  `build()` through the refactored launch helper.
- Mutation check of the new test (not part of the PR): an update that refreshes everything
  except `visible_blocks`, and a no-op update, both fail the new test in all three layouts
  (6/6 caught).

## Performance

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (NVFP4 checkpoint), 2× DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), TP=2, MTP
`num_speculative_tokens=4`, bf16 KV, vLLM 0.30.0 with this change, `max_num_seqs=64`.
Same image for both arms; the fused path was toggled at runtime by forcing
`supports_draft_decode_metadata_update` off. Averages of steady-state samples; runs per cell
in parentheses.

| concurrency | decode steps/s, stock | decode steps/s, this PR | Δ | output tok/s, stock → this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (8) | 21.93 | 22.20 | +1.2 % | 90.0 → 92.8 |
| 2 (6) | 17.7 | 18.2 | +2.8 % | 147.8 → 152.3 |
| 4 (4) | 13.4 | 13.7 | +2.2 % | 223.8 → 226.8 |
| 8 (4) | 9.73 | 9.93 | +2.1 % | 324.8 → 330.5 |
| 12 (4) | 7.75 | 7.93 | +2.3 % | 388.3 → 396.3 |
| 16 (3) | — | — | — | 439 → 440 |
| 32 (3) | — | — | — | 546 → 539 (−1.3 %) |
| 64 (3) | — | — | — | 701 → 693 (−1.1 %) |

At 2–12 concurrent requests the step-rate ranges of the two arms do not overlap. The gain
tracks the per-draft-step metadata rebuild the fused path removes: it matters when decode
steps are short and fades as they lengthen; above ~16 requests the in-place refresh on the
draft path costs slightly more than the host-side rebuild it replaces.

## Accuracy

Speculative decoding is exact; the fused path only changes when draft-step metadata is
computed. Mean acceptance length is unchanged at every concurrency (e.g. 4.13–4.26 vs
4.08–4.31 at c=2, 4.15–4.21 vs 4.16–4.21 at c=16–64), and per-position acceptance at c=64 is
0.90 / 0.83 / 0.77 / 0.68.

GSM8K (`gsm8k_cot_zeroshot`, the same 400 seeded questions in every run, thinking on,
temperature 0.6 / top-p 0.95 / top-k 20, max 32k tokens, 32 concurrent requests), two
runs per arm to measure run-to-run noise:

| run | accuracy | truncated |
|---|---|---|
| this PR #1 | 97.75 % | 0 |
| this PR #2 | 98.00 % | 0 |
| stock #1 | 97.75 % | 0 |
| stock #2 | 97.25 % | 0 |

Per question, the two runs of the same arm disagree on 8 (this PR) and 7 (stock) of the 400;
the four cross-arm pairs disagree on 8, 5, 2 and 7. Cross-arm disagreement is no larger than
within-arm disagreement, i.e. no measurable change in outputs.

## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The AI agent also ran the tests,
benchmarks and evaluations reported above, on the submitter's hardware and at the submitter's
direction. The submitter has reviewed every changed line and can answer for the change.

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @bilikaz.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

Hi @bilikaz, thanks for this PR. We hit the same cost on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next + MTP 3 (8 × A100, TP8 + EP, agentic workload at concurrency 8): in a py-spy profile of a TP worker, `_multi_step_decode > _build_uniform_attn_metadata` takes 5.2 % of the samples, and the startup log says `Attention backend(s) QWEN4_EXP_EXP_QSA_STATE cannot update draft decode metadata in place; falling back to rebuilding attention metadata eagerly.` So this change matters for us too, and I would like to help it land rather than open a competing PR.

Two notes from going through it against current main:

1. **Conflict with #64110.** #64110 (merged 30 Oct) renamed `qsa_cache.py` / `QSAStateBackend` to `common/qsa_indexer.py` / `QSAIndexerMetadataBuilder` (`QWEN4_EXP_QSA_INDEXER`). The MTP layer still owns an indexer, so on current main the drafter still falls back to the eager rebuild; `Qwen4ExpQSAMetadataBuilder` already declares the in-place update.

2. **`num_mapped_tokens` on a padded replay.** This PR stores `num_mapped_tokens = int(query_start_loc_cpu[-1])` at build time and reuses it in `update_draft_decode_metadata`. In a FULL-graph draft step the captured value is replayed for every batch padded to that size, so when the live batch has fewer real requests, the rows past the real tokens are treated as mapped (they get a request index and logical position that a rebuild would mark as padding). The slot writes are probably still harmless, but the metadata no longer equals a rebuild. Reading the count on the device from `query_start_loc[num_reqs]` inside the kernel avoids this.

I ported the idea onto the renamed builder with that device-side count, in case it is useful for your rebase: https://github.com/kimseunghyun-kr/vllm/compare/main...qsa-indexer-draft-decode-update (one commit, `e323f912dc`). It routes `build()` and `update_draft_decode_metadata()` through one writer, so the update is a rebuild of the same fields on the same device tensors; the torch fallback also takes the token-to-request map from device tensors. Its test advances `seq_lens` / slot mappings for three draft steps with one padding request and checks every field bitwise against a fresh `build()` for the raw, compressed and circular-buffer caches (the torch path passes on CPU; GPU result below).

Feel free to take any of it into this PR (a `Co-authored-by` would be nice but is not necessary). If you would prefer that I open it as a follow-up on top of yours instead, tell me. I can also run your rebased version end to end on our A100 setup.

**Update, 31 Oct: GPU run.** One A100-SXM4-40GB, `tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py`, current main (`2b009fc6d1`) against the branch (`e323f912dc`), with the compiled ops from our v0.32.0 CUDA 13 image. The 9 new cases pass: `test_qsa_indexer_draft_decode_update_matches_fresh_build` (3 cache kinds x torch / Triton) and `test_qsa_indexer_draft_decode_update_replays_in_cuda_graph` (one capture replayed over the draft steps, 3 cache kinds). Totals: main 60 passed / 14 failed, branch 69 passed / 14 failed. The 14 failures are the same tests on both (FP8 selection / sparse-attention cases and `test_qsa_unfused_cache_update_ignores_padded_qk`), so they come from this environment (sm_80 with compiled ops that are not built from main), not from the change.

(Drafted with AI assistance; I reviewed it.)

Thanks @kimseunghyun-kr, both points were right, and this is now in the PR.

#64110: merged current main. The renamed QSAIndexerMetadataBuilder now opts in.

num_mapped_tokens: fixed in 8edecd0cd. The metadata kernel now loads query_start_loc[num_reqs] itself, and the host value is gone from the kernel, the launcher and the metadata. It was actually a bit worse than a stale graph capture: the value came from the stored metadata, so even a plain update without a graph was wrong as soon as a batch was padded. I took your tests (real builder, one padding request, three draft steps, every field checked against a fresh build(), eager and from one captured CUDA graph, for the circular / compressed / uncompressed caches), with a Co-authored-by for you. On the previous commit all 6 cases fail at the first step on token_to_req. I left out the QSAMetadataInputs refactor and the torch-fallback rewrite to keep this PR small; the torch path keeps the eager rebuild (supports_draft_decode_metadata_update = HAS_TRITON). Happy to review those as a follow-up.

tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py: 80/80 pass on a GB10 (sm_121).

An end-to-end run on your A100 TP8 + EP setup would be very welcome. The drafter should no longer log the QWEN4_EXP_QSA_INDEXER ... falling back to rebuilding line, and _build_uniform_attn_metadata should drop out of the profile.

(Drafted with AI assistance; I reviewed it.)

Thanks @bilikaz, and thanks for the co-author credit. I read `8edecd0cd`: the device-side count, the shared `_launch_qsa_metadata_kernel` for `build()` and `update_draft_decode_metadata()`, and `supports_draft_decode_metadata_update = HAS_TRITON`. It looks right to me. Keeping the torch fallback and the input refactor out of this PR is fine.

I am preparing the end-to-end run on our setup (8 × A100-SXM4-40GB, TP8 + EP, MTP 3, agentic workload at concurrency 8). Base: the nightly of `2b009fc6d1`, which has #64110 and the same `qsa_indexer.py` as your merge base. Both arms also have our GDN capture PRs (#61779/#61952), and your two files are taken unchanged from `c98d5a23ed`. I will check that the fallback log line appears only without the PR, compare TTFT/TPOT, and run a py-spy profile of both arms to see whether `_build_uniform_attn_metadata` drops out. I will post the results here.

(Drafted with AI assistance; I reviewed it.)

End-to-end result on our setup, as promised. Setup: 8 × A100-SXM4-40GB, TP8 + EP, MTP 3, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, agentic workload at concurrency 8, nightly `2b009fc6d1` + #61779/#61952 in both arms. The treatment arm adds your two files unchanged from `c98d5a23ed`. One job on one node (26077310), 1 Nov.

**The in-place update is used.** `QWEN4_EXP_QSA_INDEXER cannot update draft decode metadata in place; falling back to rebuilding attention metadata eagerly.` appears in both control-arm start-up logs. It does not appear in either arm with the PR.

**Host profile.** py-spy at 50 Hz for 300 s on all 8 TP workers. Each value is the median share of samples over the 8 workers, about 9,050 samples per worker. The min–max ranges of the two arms do not overlap on any of these rows.

| Share of worker samples | Without PR | With PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| MTP `propose` | 8.7 % | 2.2 % |
| `_build_uniform_attn_metadata` | 5.3 % | 0 % |
| `build_attn_metadata` (all) | 15.9 % | 12.1 % |
| `sample_tokens` | 15.3 % | 8.8 % |
| idle, waiting for the scheduler | 55.3 % | 62.1 % |

`_launch_qsa_metadata_kernel` costs 0.2 %.

**Serving, 30 min per arm (control first).** Both arms: 0 failed samples.

| | Without PR | With PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| TTFT P50 / P95 | 409 / 830 ms | 404 / 834 ms |
| TPOT P50 / P95 | 7.29 / 10.93 ms | 7.25 / 10.68 ms |
| Output throughput | 593 tok/s | 579 tok/s |

All differences are inside the run-to-run spread we measured on this setup (two runs of one configuration: TPOT P50 7.23 vs 7.30 ms, 582 vs 575 tok/s). At C8 our decode steps are GPU-bound, and the worker host time is mostly hidden. So the saved host time does not show as a latency change here. A configuration where the host is the limit (more concurrency, or a faster GPU) is more likely to show it.

**Accuracy.** Paired per turn on the 2,170 turns that both arms scored: 0.5673 without the PR, 0.5655 with it. The difference is −0.002, 95 % bootstrap CI [−0.022, +0.018]. Generation is sampled, so 37 % of turns differ between the arms. The same spread occurs between two runs of one server.

**Update: concurrency 32 (job 26082678).** Same two servers. The arms ran in both orders (without, with, with, without), 30 min each, 0 failed samples. The fallback log line again appears only without the PR.

| Order | Arm | TTFT P50 / P95 | TPOT P50 / P95 | Output throughput |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | without PR | 3,480 / 28,300 ms | 19.6 / 51.5 ms | 599 tok/s |
| 1 | with PR | 3,813 / 27,366 ms | 19.8 / 49.1 ms | 607 tok/s |
| 2 | with PR | 4,104 / 25,210 ms | 21.1 / 51.5 ms | 588 tok/s |
| 2 | without PR | 3,544 / 25,900 ms | 20.9 / 49.8 ms | 602 tok/s |

No difference is beyond noise. The TTFT P50 difference (+329 / +576 ms) has a 95 % CI of about ±2.5–3 s when resampled by conversation, the same width as the difference between the two runs without the PR. Paired accuracy: +0.014 [−0.003, +0.031] and −0.007 [−0.024, +0.011].

This setup does not make the host the limit at C32. It has no CPU KV offload. The KV cache stays about 90 % full, about 10 requests wait, throughput stays at about 600 tok/s (the same as at C8), and TTFT grows during the run. The PR makes the KV cache 0.19 % smaller (1,131,643 vs 1,133,761 tokens) and does not change the queue. So on 8 × A100 we see less host time per worker and no latency change at C8 or C32. A setup where the host limits the step time would be needed to see a latency gain.

(Drafted with AI assistance; I reviewed it.)

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

+def _draft_indexer_builder(cache_kind: str, device: torch.device):
+    if cache_kind == "circular":
+        spec = CircularBufferSpec(
+            block_size=_DRAFT_RING_CAPACITY,
+            num_kv_heads=1,
+            head_size=64,
+            head_size_v=0,
+            dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        )
+    else:
+        spec = MLAAttentionSpec(
+            block_size=_DRAFT_BLOCK_SIZE,
+            num_kv_heads=1,
+            head_size=64,
+            dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            tokens_per_state=_DRAFT_COMPRESS_RATIO if cache_kind == "compressed" else 1,
+        )
+    config = SimpleNamespace(
+        scheduler_config=SimpleNamespace(
+            max_num_batched_tokens=64, max_num_seqs=_DRAFT_NUM_REQUESTS
+        ),
+        speculative_config=None,
+        parallel_config=SimpleNamespace(decode_context_parallel_size=1),
+    )
+    return QSAIndexerMetadataBuilder(spec, ["indexer"], config, device)
+
+
+def _draft_decode_batch(
+    seq_lens: list[int], block_table: torch.Tensor
+) -> SimpleNamespace:
+    """One query token per request; trailing zero lengths are padding."""
+    num_live = sum(seq_len > 0 for seq_len in seq_lens)
+    assert all(seq_len > 0 for seq_len in seq_lens[:num_live])
+    query_start_loc = torch.tensor(
+        [min(request, num_live) for request in range(len(seq_lens) + 1)],
+        dtype=torch.int32,
+    )
+    # The runner's group slots for the token at position seq_len - 1.
+    slots = [
+        int(block_table[request, (seq_len - 1) // _DRAFT_BLOCK_SIZE])
+        * _DRAFT_BLOCK_SIZE
+        + (seq_len - 1) % _DRAFT_BLOCK_SIZE
+        if seq_len > 0
+        else -1
+        for request, seq_len in enumerate(seq_lens)
+    ]
+    device = block_table.device
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        num_actual_tokens=len(seq_lens),
+        num_reqs=len(seq_lens),
+        max_query_len=1,
+        max_seq_len=_DRAFT_MAX_SEQ_LEN,
+        query_start_loc=query_start_loc.to(device),
+        query_start_loc_cpu=query_start_loc,
+        seq_lens=torch.tensor(seq_lens, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
+        slot_mapping=torch.tensor(slots, dtype=torch.int64, device=device),
+        block_table_tensor=block_table.clone(),
+    )
+
+
+def _check_draft_steps_match_fresh_builds(cache_kind: str, run_update) -> None:
+    """Advance the runner buffers like a speculator and compare after updates."""
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    captured_table = torch.arange(1, 17, dtype=torch.int32, device=device).view(4, 4)
+    replayed_table = torch.arange(32, 16, -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    replayed_table = replayed_table.view(4, 4)
+    replayed_table[-1] = 0  # The padding request sits on the null block.
+    builder = _draft_indexer_builder(cache_kind, device)
+    captured = _draft_decode_batch(_DRAFT_CAPTURED_SEQ_LENS, captured_table)
+    metadata = builder.build(0, captured)
+    run_update = run_update(builder, metadata)
+
+    for seq_lens in _DRAFT_REPLAYED_SEQ_LENS:
+        step = _draft_decode_batch(seq_lens, replayed_table)
+        # The replayed step arrives through the captured persistent buffers.
+        for name in ("query_start_loc", "seq_lens", "slot_mapping"):
+            getattr(captured, name).copy_(getattr(step, name))
+        captured.block_table_tensor.copy_(step.block_table_tensor)
+        run_update()
+
+        expected = _draft_indexer_builder(cache_kind, device).build(0, step)
+        for field in dataclasses.fields(expected):
+            actual_value = getattr(metadata, field.name)
+            expected_value = getattr(expected, field.name)
+            if isinstance(expected_value, torch.Tensor):
+                assert torch.equal(actual_value, expected_value), field.name
+            else:
+                assert actual_value == expected_value, field.name
+
+
+@requires_qsa_kernels
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("cache_kind", ["circular", "compressed", "uncompressed"])
+def test_qsa_indexer_draft_decode_update_matches_fresh_build(cache_kind: str) -> None:
+    assert QSAIndexerMetadataBuilder.supports_draft_decode_metadata_update
+
+    def eager_update(builder, metadata):
+        return lambda: builder.update_draft_decode_metadata(metadata)
+
+    _check_draft_steps_match_fresh_builds(cache_kind, eager_update)
+
+
+@requires_qsa_kernels
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("cache_kind", ["circular", "compressed", "uncompressed"])
+def test_qsa_indexer_draft_decode_update_replays_in_cuda_graph(
+    cache_kind: str,
+) -> None:
+    """The update must be capturable: one capture serves every replayed step."""
+
+    def capture_update(builder, metadata):
+        # Compile the Triton kernel before capture.
+        builder.update_draft_decode_metadata(metadata)
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+            builder.update_draft_decode_metadata(metadata)
+        return graph.replay
+
+    _check_draft_steps_match_fresh_builds(cache_kind, capture_update)
+
+
 @requires_qsa_kernels

Hi @bilikaz, thanks for this PR. We hit the same cost on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next + MTP 3 (8 × A100, TP8 + EP, agentic workload at concurrency 8): in a py-spy profile of a TP worker, `_multi_step_decode > _build_uniform_attn_metadata` takes 5.2 % of the samples, and the startup log says `Attention backend(s) QWEN4_EXP_EXP_QSA_STATE cannot update draft decode metadata in place; falling back to rebuilding attention metadata eagerly.` So this change matters for us too, and I would like to help it land rather than open a competing PR.

Two notes from going through it against current main:

1. **Conflict with #64110.** #64110 (merged 30 Oct) renamed `qsa_cache.py` / `QSAStateBackend` to `common/qsa_indexer.py` / `QSAIndexerMetadataBuilder` (`QWEN4_EXP_QSA_INDEXER`). The MTP layer still owns an indexer, so on current main the drafter still falls back to the eager rebuild; `Qwen4ExpQSAMetadataBuilder` already declares the in-place update.

2. **`num_mapped_tokens` on a padded replay.** This PR stores `num_mapped_tokens = int(query_start_loc_cpu[-1])` at build time and reuses it in `update_draft_decode_metadata`. In a FULL-graph draft step the captured value is replayed for every batch padded to that size, so when the live batch has fewer real requests, the rows past the real tokens are treated as mapped (they get a request index and logical position that a rebuild would mark as padding). The slot writes are probably still harmless, but the metadata no longer equals a rebuild. Reading the count on the device from `query_start_loc[num_reqs]` inside the kernel avoids this.

I ported the idea onto the renamed builder with that device-side count, in case it is useful for your rebase: https://github.com/kimseunghyun-kr/vllm/compare/main...qsa-indexer-draft-decode-update (one commit, `e323f912dc`). It routes `build()` and `update_draft_decode_metadata()` through one writer, so the update is a rebuild of the same fields on the same device tensors; the torch fallback also takes the token-to-request map from device tensors. Its test advances `seq_lens` / slot mappings for three draft steps with one padding request and checks every field bitwise against a fresh `build()` for the raw, compressed and circular-buffer caches (the torch path passes on CPU; GPU result below).

Feel free to take any of it into this PR (a `Co-authored-by` would be nice but is not necessary). If you would prefer that I open it as a follow-up on top of yours instead, tell me. I can also run your rebased version end to end on our A100 setup.

**Update, 31 Oct: GPU run.** One A100-SXM4-40GB, `tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py`, current main (`2b009fc6d1`) against the branch (`e323f912dc`), with the compiled ops from our v0.32.0 CUDA 13 image. The 9 new cases pass: `test_qsa_indexer_draft_decode_update_matches_fresh_build` (3 cache kinds x torch / Triton) and `test_qsa_indexer_draft_decode_update_replays_in_cuda_graph` (one capture replayed over the draft steps, 3 cache kinds). Totals: main 60 passed / 14 failed, branch 69 passed / 14 failed. The 14 failures are the same tests on both (FP8 selection / sparse-attention cases and `test_qsa_unfused_cache_update_ignores_padded_qk`), so they come from this environment (sm_80 with compiled ops that are not built from main), not from the change.

Thanks @kimseunghyun-kr, both points were right, and this is now in the PR.

#64110: merged current main. The renamed QSAIndexerMetadataBuilder now opts in.

num_mapped_tokens: fixed in 8edecd0cd. The metadata kernel now loads query_start_loc[num_reqs] itself, and the host value is gone from the kernel, the launcher and the metadata. It was actually a bit worse than a stale graph capture: the value came from the stored metadata, so even a plain update without a graph was wrong as soon as a batch was padded. I took your tests (real builder, one padding request, three draft steps, every field checked against a fresh build(), eager and from one captured CUDA graph, for the circular / compressed / uncompressed caches), with a Co-authored-by for you. On the previous commit all 6 cases fail at the first step on token_to_req. I left out the QSAMetadataInputs refactor and the torch-fallback rewrite to keep this PR small; the torch path keeps the eager rebuild (supports_draft_decode_metadata_update = HAS_TRITON). Happy to review those as a follow-up.

tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py: 80/80 pass on a GB10 (sm_121).

An end-to-end run on your A100 TP8 + EP setup would be very welcome. The drafter should no longer log the QWEN4_EXP_QSA_INDEXER ... falling back to rebuilding line, and _build_uniform_attn_metadata should drop out of the profile.

Thanks @bilikaz, and thanks for the co-author credit. I read `8edecd0cd`: the device-side count, the shared `_launch_qsa_metadata_kernel` for `build()` and `update_draft_decode_metadata()`, and `supports_draft_decode_metadata_update = HAS_TRITON`. It looks right to me. Keeping the torch fallback and the input refactor out of this PR is fine.

I am preparing the end-to-end run on our setup (8 × A100-SXM4-40GB, TP8 + EP, MTP 3, agentic workload at concurrency 8). Base: the nightly of `2b009fc6d1`, which has #64110 and the same `qsa_indexer.py` as your merge base. Both arms also have our GDN capture PRs (#61779/#61952), and your two files are taken unchanged from `c98d5a23ed`. I will check that the fallback log line appears only without the PR, compare TTFT/TPOT, and run a py-spy profile of both arms to see whether `_build_uniform_attn_metadata` drops out. (Drafted with AI assistance; I reviewed it.)

End-to-end result on our setup, as promised. Setup: 8 × A100-SXM4-40GB, TP8 + EP, MTP 3, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, agentic workload at concurrency 8, nightly `2b009fc6d1` + #61779/#61952 in both arms. The treatment arm adds your two files unchanged from `c98d5a23ed`. One job on one node (26077310), 1 Nov.

**The in-place update is used.** `QWEN4_EXP_QSA_INDEXER cannot update draft decode metadata in place; falling back to rebuilding attention metadata eagerly.` appears in both control-arm start-up logs. It does not appear in either arm with the PR.

**Host profile.** py-spy at 50 Hz for 300 s on all 8 TP workers. Each value is the median share of samples over the 8 workers, about 9,050 samples per worker. The min–max ranges of the two arms do not overlap on any of these rows.

| Share of worker samples | Without PR | With PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| MTP `propose` | 8.7 % | 2.2 % |
| `_build_uniform_attn_metadata` | 5.3 % | 0 % |
| `build_attn_metadata` (all) | 15.9 % | 12.1 % |
| `sample_tokens` | 15.3 % | 8.8 % |
| idle, waiting for the scheduler | 55.3 % | 62.1 % |

`_launch_qsa_metadata_kernel` costs 0.2 %.

**Serving, 30 min per arm (control first).** Both arms: 0 failed samples.

| | Without PR | With PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| TTFT P50 / P95 | 409 / 830 ms | 404 / 834 ms |
| TPOT P50 / P95 | 7.29 / 10.93 ms | 7.25 / 10.68 ms |
| Output throughput | 593 tok/s | 579 tok/s |

All differences are inside the run-to-run spread we measured on this setup (two runs of one configuration: TPOT P50 7.23 vs 7.30 ms, 582 vs 575 tok/s). At C8 our decode steps are GPU-bound, and the worker host time is mostly hidden. So the saved host time does not show as a latency change here. A configuration where the host is the limit (more concurrency, or a faster GPU) is more likely to show it.

**Accuracy.** Paired per turn on the 2,170 turns that both arms scored: 0.5673 without the PR, 0.5655 with it. The difference is −0.002, 95 % bootstrap CI [−0.022, +0.018]. Generation is sampled, so 37 % of turns differ between the arms. The same spread occurs between two runs of one server.

**Update: concurrency 32 (job 26082678).** Same two servers. The arms ran in both orders (without, with, with, without), 30 min each, 0 failed samples. The fallback log line again appears only without the PR.

| Order | Arm | TTFT P50 / P95 | TPOT P50 / P95 | Output throughput |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | without PR | 3,480 / 28,300 ms | 19.6 / 51.5 ms | 599 tok/s |
| 1 | with PR | 3,813 / 27,366 ms | 19.8 / 49.1 ms | 607 tok/s |
| 2 | with PR | 4,104 / 25,210 ms | 21.1 / 51.5 ms | 588 tok/s |
| 2 | without PR | 3,544 / 25,900 ms | 20.9 / 49.8 ms | 602 tok/s |

No difference is beyond noise. The TTFT P50 difference (+329 / +576 ms) has a 95 % CI of about ±2.5–3 s when resampled by conversation, the same width as the difference between the two runs without the PR. Paired accuracy: +0.014 [−0.003, +0.031] and −0.007 [−0.024, +0.011].

This setup does not make the host the limit at C32. It has no CPU KV offload. The KV cache stays about 90 % full, about 10 requests wait, throughput stays at about 600 tok/s (the same as at C8), and TTFT grows during the run. The PR makes the KV cache 0.19 % smaller (1,131,643 vs 1,133,761 tokens) and does not change the queue. So on 8 × A100 we see less host time per worker and no latency change at C8 or C32. A setup where the host limits the step time would be needed to see a latency gain.
